verses.jalalayn: ﻿The Clattering Blow, the Resurrection that will make hearts clatter by its terrors.

﻿What is the Clattering Blow? — [intended] to emphasise its awesomeness (mā’l-qāri‘a: both of these [elements] constitute a subject and a predicate, and [together] the predicate of [the first] al-qāri‘a).

verses.saheeh: And what can make you know what is the Striking Calamity?
verses.khattab: And what will make you realize what the Striking Disaster is
verses.jalalayn: ﻿And what will show you, [what] will make known to you, what the Clattering Blow is? — additional emphasis of its awesomeness (the first mā is a subject, and what follows it is its predicate; the second mā and its predicate also function together as the second direct object of [the verb] adrā, ‘show’).
verses.romanUrdu: Tum kya jano ke woh azeem hadisa kya hai

verses.saheeh: It is the Day when people will be like moths, dispersed,
verses.khattab: ˹It is˺ the Day people will be like scattered moths
verses.jalalayn: ﻿The day (yawma: that which renders it accusative is [the verb] indicated by al-qāri‘a, in other words, [by the implied] taqra‘u, ‘it clatters’) mankind will be like scattered moths, like a throng of scattered locusts surging into each other in confusion, until they are summoned to the Reckoning,
verses.romanUrdu: woh din jab log bhikre huey parwano ki tarah

verses.saheeh: And the mountains will be like wool, fluffed up.
verses.khattab: and the mountains will be like carded wool
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and the mountains will be like tufts of wool, like carded wool in terms of the lightness with which it floats [in the air] until it comes to settle upon the earth.
verses.romanUrdu: Aur pahad rang bi rangi dhunki hui oon ke tarah hongey

verses.saheeh: Then as for one whose scales are heavy [with good deeds],
verses.khattab: So as for those whose scale is heavy ˹with good deeds˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Then as for him whose scales weigh heavy, in that his good deeds outweigh his misdeeds,

verses.saheeh: He will be in a pleasant life.
verses.khattab: they will be in a life of bliss
verses.jalalayn: ﻿he will enjoy a pleasant life, in Paradise, that is to say, a pleasing one, for he will be pleased with it, that is, it will be pleasing to him;
verses.romanUrdu: Woh dil pasand aish mei hoga

verses.saheeh: But as for one whose scales are light,
verses.khattab: And as for those whose scale is light
verses.jalalayn: ﻿but as for him whose scales weigh light, in that his evil deeds outweigh his good ones,
verses.romanUrdu: Aur jis kay palade halke hongey

verses.saheeh: His refuge will be an abyss.
verses.khattab: their home will be the abyss
verses.romanUrdu: Uski jaye qarar gehri khayi hogi

verses.saheeh: And what can make you know what that is?
verses.khattab: And what will make you realize what that is
verses.jalalayn: ﻿And what will show you what it is?, that is to say, what the Abyss is.
verses.romanUrdu: Aur tumhein kya khabar kay woh kya cheez hai

verses.saheeh: It is a Fire, intensely hot.
verses.jalalayn: ﻿It is: A scorching fire, of extremely hot temperature (the hā’ of hiya is for [consonantal] quiescence, and is retained when reciting without a [subsequent] pause or with; some omit it when reciting without a pause).
